keywords.def: a particular way of thinking about something
a natural ability or potential to learn something
the possibility of developing into something greater or better
to understand or explain the meaning of something
a particular method or way of dealing with something
to change your approach to suit a new situation
information about your performance that helps you improve

sentences.en: Some people see failure as proof that they aren’t good at something.
sentences.zh: 有些人把失败视为自己不擅长某事的证明。

sentences.en: Others see it as an opportunity to improve.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则将其视为提升的机遇。

sentences.en: Why? Today I want to try and answer this question by thinking about “growth mindsets”.
sentences.zh: 为什么？今天，我想通过思考“成长型思维”来尝试回答这个问题。

sentences.en: The growth mindset concept suggests that our abilities aren’t completely fixed, and that we can improve through practice and effort.
sentences.zh: 成长型思维的概念表明，我们的能力并不是完全固定不变的，我们可以通过练习和努力来取得进步。

sentences.en: We are going to look at what a growth mindset means, how it affects learning, and why it can be particularly important when learning a language.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨什么是成长型思维，它如何影响学习，以及为什么它在学习一门语言时尤为重要。

sentences.en: And at the same time, we will practice our English listening comprehension and learn some new vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 同时，我们还将练习英语听力理解并学习一些新词汇！

sentences.en: What is a growth mindset? A mindset is a particular way of thinking about something.
sentences.zh: 什么是成长型思维？思维方式（mindset）是对某事物的特定思考方式。

sentences.en: Mindset includes the beliefs and attitudes that we have, and these beliefs can influence how we behave.
sentences.zh: 思维方式包括我们拥有的信念和态度，而这些信念会影响我们的行为方式。

sentences.en: An example of a mindset is a “positive mindset “.
sentences.zh: 思维方式的一个例子就是“积极的思维方式”。

sentences.en: If you have a positive mindset, you are thinking positively, optimistically about something.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有积极的思维方式，你就会对某事抱有积极、乐观的看法。

sentences.en: For this episode, though, the two key concepts are “fixed mindsets” and “growth mindsets “.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于本期节目而言，两个核心概念是“固定型思维”和“成长型思维”。

sentences.en: A person with a fixed mindset tends to believe that ability is fixed or relatively fixed.
sentences.zh: 拥有固定型思维的人往往认为能力是固定或相对固定的。

sentences.en: They might believe things like your intelligence or your creativity are things that you are born with.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会认为，诸如智力或创造力之类的事情是你生来就有的。

sentences.en: You either have talent or you don’t have talent for something.
sentences.zh: 你要么有天赋，要么在这方面没有天赋。

sentences.en: This can be true for language ability. Some people with fixed mindsets believe that the ability to learn a language is also fixed.
sentences.zh: 这对于语言能力来说也是如此。一些持有固定型思维的人认为，学习语言的能力也是固定的。

sentences.en: I’m sure some of you have this mindset now.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，你们现在有些人就有这种思维方式。

sentences.en: Perhaps you think something like, “I have a terrible memory, so I’ll never learn vocabulary.”
sentences.zh: 也许你会想：“我记性太差了，所以永远也学不会词汇。”

sentences.en: That statement, “I’ll never learn vocabulary,” doesn’t just describe your current ability.
sentences.zh: 那句话——“我永远也学不会词汇”——不仅仅是在描述你当前的能力。

sentences.en: It suggests that you think your ability is permanent.
sentences.zh: 它暗示你认为自己的能力是永久性的。

sentences.en: You’re never going to be able to learn vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 你将永远无法学会词汇。

sentences.en: If you believe you aren’t naturally good at languages and you can’t improve, you’re going to spend less time practicing, and you’re going to be less optimistic about your future.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为自己天生不擅长语言且无法进步，你花在练习上的时间就会减少，而且你对未来的看法也会不那么乐观。

sentences.en: Someone with a growth mindset believes that abilities can develop and improve.
sentences.zh: 拥有成长型思维的人则认为能力是可以发展和提升的。

sentences.en: It’s the opposite to a fixed mindset. Fixed mindset… your ability is fixed.
sentences.zh: 这与固定型思维恰恰相反。固定型思维……你的能力是固定的。

sentences.en: It’s static. You have what you have. You can’t improve it.
sentences.zh: 它是静止的。你有什么样的能力就是什么样的。你无法提升它。

sentences.en: Whereas a growth mindset believes that your ability can change.
sentences.zh: 而成长型思维则认为你的能力是可以改变的。

sentences.en: Your ability can improve, or it can get worse, I guess, but it can also improve.
sentences.zh: 你的能力可以提升，或者我想它也可能会变差，但它确实可以提升。

sentences.en: Being bad at something right now doesn’t mean you’re going to be bad at it forever.
sentences.zh: 现在不擅长某事并不意味着你永远都会不擅长。

sentences.en: Your ability can change and will change.
sentences.zh: 你的能力可以改变，也将会改变。

sentences.en: This might sound a little bit like being an optimist or a pessimist.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点像是乐天派或悲观派。

sentences.en: Optimists think things will be better. Pessimists think things will be worse in the future.
sentences.zh: 乐天派认为事情会变好。悲观派则认为未来事情会变糟。

sentences.en: But I think it’s a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这略有不同。

sentences.en: The main difference between growth and fixed mindsets is how you interpret, how you understand, your ability.
sentences.zh: 成长型思维和固定型思维的主要区别在于你如何诠释、如何理解自己的能力。

sentences.en: People have different abilities. That is undeniable.
sentences.zh: 人们的能力各不相同。这是不可否认的。

sentences.en: People have different natural abilities, circumstances, opportunities, limitations.
sentences.zh: 人们拥有不同的天赋、环境、机遇和局限性。

sentences.en: This is the case. I made an episode a few months ago on talent, where I talked about the differences between talent and skill and ability and opportunity.
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此。几个月前我做过一期关于天赋的节目，我在节目中探讨了天赋、技能、能力和机遇之间的区别。

sentences.en: The most important thing you can take away from today’s episode is that your current ability is not necessarily the limit of your ability, right?
sentences.zh: 你能从今天的节目中带走的最重要的东西是，你当前的能力并不一定是你能力的极限，对吧？

sentences.en: That your current level right now, your current abilities right now is not necessarily the limit.
sentences.zh: 你眼下的当前水平、你眼下的当前能力并不一定是极限。

sentences.en: You can get better. And that is the core belief behind the idea of a growth mindset.
sentences.zh: 你可以变得更好。这就是成长型思维背后的核心信念。

sentences.en: We all know people who seem to be naturally good at things.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道有些人似乎天生就擅长各种事物。

sentences.en: We’re all language learners here. I’m a Japanese learner.
sentences.zh: 我们这里都是语言学习者。我是一个日语学习者。

sentences.en: Some people just seem to pick up languages really quickly and naturally.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎就是能非常迅速且自然地学会语言。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, I am not one of these people.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我不是这类人。

sentences.en: I’ve been learning Japanese for 10 years now.
sentences.zh: 我学日语已经有 10 年了。

sentences.en: Aptitude is a term for a person’s natural ability, or I guess their potential to learn something.
sentences.zh: 才能（Aptitude）是指一个人天生的能力，或者说是我所理解的他们学习某事物的潜力。

sentences.en: In language learning, in English learning, some people find it easier to remember vocabulary than other people.
sentences.zh: 在语言学习、英语学习中，有些人比其他人更容易记住词汇。

sentences.en: They have a natural aptitude for remembering vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 他们天生就具有记忆词汇的才能。

sentences.en: But having different levels of aptitude doesn’t mean that ability is fixed.
sentences.zh: 但是，拥有不同的才能水平并不意味着能力是固定的。

sentences.en: There are people who seem to learn foreign languages very quickly.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎能非常快地学会外语。

sentences.en: Other people seem to need more time. But just because you struggle at the beginning, it doesn’t mean you’re going to struggle learning forever.
sentences.zh: 另一些人似乎需要更多时间。但仅仅因为你刚开始时感到吃力，并不意味着你永远都会学得很吃力。

sentences.en: Your ability can develop and can improve with practice and experience.
sentences.zh: 通过练习和经验，你的能力是可以发展和提升的。

sentences.en: Another common belief around learning languages and abilities is to do with age.
sentences.zh: 关于语言学习和能力的另一个普遍观点与年龄有关。

sentences.en: There is certainly evidence that age can affect language learning, particularly pronunciation and some aspects of grammar as well.
sentences.zh: 确实有证据表明年龄会影响语言学习，特别是发音以及语法的某些方面。

sentences.en: Children seem to be better at learning things like pronunciation and those grammar aspects.
sentences.zh: 孩子们似乎更擅长学习发音和那些语法方面的东西。

sentences.en: But this doesn’t mean that adults are incapable of becoming highly proficient.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着成年人就无法变得高度精通。

sentences.en: Of course they are. Adults are able to become fluent in language.
sentences.zh: 当然不是。成年人完全能够流利掌握一门语言。

sentences.en: Your belief about your language ability isn’t actually one belief.
sentences.zh: 你对自身语言能力的信念其实并非单一的信念。

sentences.en: Research has suggested that people hold beliefs in different areas.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，人们在不同领域持有不同的信念。

sentences.en: They have different mindsets for different parts of their learning ability, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，对于他们学习能力的各个部分，他们有不同的思维方式。

sentences.en: People hold beliefs on their general language ability.
sentences.zh: 人们对自己的整体语言能力持有信念。

sentences.en: This is whether your ability to communicate can change.
sentences.zh: 这关乎你沟通能力是否能够改变。

sentences.en: They also hold beliefs on their aptitude for learning languages, and on things like how age affects learning.
sentences.zh: 他们也对学习语言的才能以及年龄如何影响学习等方面持有信念。

sentences.en: People can have a fixed mindset on one of those areas and a growth mindset on another area.
sentences.zh: 人们可能在其中一个领域持有固定型思维，而在另一个领域持有成长型思维。

sentences.en: It’s not as simple as just being a, a fixed mindset or a growth mindset person.
sentences.zh: 事情并没有“单纯是一个固定型思维的人或一个成长型思维的人”那么简单。

sentences.en: In fact, research published by Lou, Chaffee, and Noels in the journal called Studies in Second Language Acquisition found that only 20% of language learners had a clearly growth-oriented mindset, while another 20% had a clearly fixed mindset.
sentences.zh: 事实上，由 Lou、Chaffee 和 Noels 发表在《Studies in Second Language Acquisition》杂志上的研究发现，只有 20% 的语言学习者具有明确的成长导向思维，而另外 20% 的人则具有明确的固定型思维。

sentences.en: That means that the majority of language learners, about 60% of all language learners, have a mixed mindset.
sentences.zh: 这意味着大多数语言学习者，大约 60% 的语言学习者，都具有混合型的思维方式。

sentences.en: I don’t find this surprising. There are a lot of people who believe that they can improve certain parts of their ability in language learning, but also that they can’t improve parts of their language learning.
sentences.zh: 对此我并不感到惊奇。有很多人认为他们可以提升语言学习中能力的某些部分，但同时也认为自己无法提升语言学习的其他部分。

sentences.en: I’m an example of this. I have a growth mindset when it comes to things like vocabulary, and when it comes to things like grammar acquisition.
sentences.zh: 我就是一个例子。在词汇之类的事情以及语法习得之类的事情上，我有成长型思维。

sentences.en: But I have a bit more of a fixed mindset when it comes to my writing ability in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 但在我的日语写作能力方面，我则稍微偏向固定型思维。

sentences.en: It’s something that I don’t practice much because I don’t necessarily believe I can become good at it.
sentences.zh: 这是一项我不太练习的技能，因为我并不认为自己能够在这方面变得优秀。

sentences.en: I know if I had a growth mindset and I dedicated my time and practice and effort, I would become better.
sentences.zh: 我知道，如果我有成长型思维，并且投入时间、练习和努力，我会变得更好。

sentences.en: I would develop the ability. But just naturally, I have a fixed mindset on that regard, and it’s something I need to change.
sentences.zh: 我会培养出这种能力。但就天性而言，我在那方面有着固定型思维，而这是我需要改变的地方。

sentences.en: We’ll talk about it later. You can change your mindset, of course.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会谈到这一点。当然，你可以改变自己的思维方式。

sentences.en: Does having different beliefs about your abilities change the way you learn?
sentences.zh: 对自己的能力持有不同的信念会改变你的学习方式吗？

sentences.en: Well, the answer is potentially yes. Not definitely yes, but potentially yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，答案是潜在的会。不是绝对会，但潜在的会。

sentences.en: Our mindset can influence how we respond to challenges and how we respond to the mistakes we make.
sentences.zh: 我们的思维方式会影响我们如何应对挑战以及如何对待我们犯下的错误。

sentences.en: A learner with a more fixed mindset might see a disappointing result, maybe you fail a test, and then they use that disappointing result as evidence they don’t have the correct ability, or they don’t have the ability to succeed.
sentences.zh: 一个具有更多固定型思维的学习者可能会看到令人失望的结果，比如你考试不及格，然后他们就会把这个令人失望的结果当作证据，证明自己没有正确的能力，或者没有成功的才能。

sentences.en: They might decide that there is no point in trying anymore because they are not naturally talented at that aspect of language learning.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会认为再怎么努力也没有意义，因为他们在语言学习的这一方面没有天生才华。

sentences.en: But if you have a growth mindset, so the opposite type of mindset, you can get a similar result, a failure in a test, but you use that to improve.
sentences.zh: 但如果你拥有成长型思维——也就是相反类型的思维方式，你可能会得到相似的结果（比如考试失败），但你会利用这一点来改进。

sentences.en: You ask for feedback and you change your study methods.
sentences.zh: 你寻求反馈并改变你的学习方法。

sentences.en: You practice more, work more, and you can improve.
sentences.zh: 你多加练习，付出更多努力，然后你就能取得进步。

sentences.en: Basically, failure can have a different meaning for everyone.
sentences.zh: 基本上，失败对每个人来说可以有不同的意义。

sentences.en: If you have a fixed mindset, failure can feel like a judgment of your ability.
sentences.zh: 如果你有固定型思维，失败会感觉像是对你能力的一种评判。

sentences.en: You fail an exam, or you have a bad performance in a conversation, or you write a essay which your teacher says is not very good, and you take that as a judgment on your ability.
sentences.zh: 你考试不及格，或者在对话中表现不佳，或者写了一篇老师说不太好的论文，你就会把这当作对你能力的一场审判。

sentences.en: But if you have a growth mindset, the failure, the bad result, is just information to help you improve.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有成长型思维，失败、不好的结果就只是一种帮助你改进的信息。

sentences.en: Mindset can also affect the kind of challenges that people are willing to take.
sentences.zh: 思维方式还会影响人们愿意接受什么样的挑战。

sentences.en: When you believe your ability is fixed, when you believe you can’t improve your natural ability, challenging tasks feel really threatening, right?
sentences.zh: 当你相信自己的能力是固定的时候，当你相信自己无法提升天生能力时，具有挑战性的任务就会让人感觉非常具有威胁性，对吧？

sentences.en: They create a risk of failure, and failure makes you feel bad.
sentences.zh: 它们会带来失败的风险，而失败会让你感觉糟糕。

sentences.en: Failure makes you feel like you’re not talented enough.
sentences.zh: 失败会让你觉得自己的才华不够。

sentences.en: People with growth mindsets, of course, don’t like failing.
sentences.zh: 当然，拥有成长型思维的人也不喜欢失败。

sentences.en: Failure is still frustrating. But if you have a growth mindset, you’re less likely to see one failure as proof that you should give up.
sentences.zh: 失败仍然是令人沮丧的。但如果你有成长型思维，你就较少会把一次失败当作你应该放弃的证据。

sentences.en: This is particularly important for language learners.
sentences.zh: 这对于语言学习者来说尤为重要。

sentences.en: You’re going to make mistakes. Of course you are.
sentences.zh: 你会犯错。你当然会。

sentences.en: If you interpret every mistake you make as evidence that you’re bad at English, learning English is not going to be fun for you.
sentences.zh: 如果你把犯下的每一个错误都解读为你英语不好的证据，那么学习英语对你来说就不会是一件快乐的事。

sentences.en: But if you treat your mistakes as just as part of learning, then they give you useful information.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把错误当作学习的一部分来对待，那么它们就会为你提供有用的信息。

sentences.en: They help you improve. Having a growth mindset is not the same thing as believing that working harder will make you better.
sentences.zh: 它们能帮你取得进步。拥有成长型思维并不等于相信“付出更多努力就会变得更好”。

sentences.en: They’re often connected, but it’s not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 它们通常是相连的，但并非同一回事。

sentences.en: Working harder does not always make you better.
sentences.zh: 付出更多努力并不总是能让你变得更好。

sentences.en: You’ve probably heard the cliché … “work smarter, not harder “.
sentences.zh: 你可能听过那个陈词滥调……“要巧干，不要苦干”。

sentences.en: It’s quite a cliché, but there is some truth there.
sentences.zh: 这虽然是个老生常谈，但其中确实蕴含着一些真理。

sentences.en: If you’re really struggling with something, doing exactly the same thing for twice as long might not help you.
sentences.zh: 如果你在某事上真的很挣扎，用完全相同的方法花上两倍的时间可能并无帮助。

sentences.en: Sometimes you need to change how you’re studying, how you’re learning.
sentences.zh: 有时你需要改变学习和吸收知识的方式。

sentences.en: For example, I have, in the past, spent hours every day memorizing long lists of vocabulary, and then I still forgot all of the words I tried to remember.
sentences.zh: 例如，我过去曾花费每天数小时的时间背诵长长的词汇表，结果我还是忘光了所有试图记住的单词。

sentences.en: Working harder there was not the answer.
sentences.zh: 在那裡，一味地死记硬背并不是答案。

sentences.en: Spending two hours remembering lists of vocabulary was not going to help me learn Japanese faster.
sentences.zh: 花两个小时背诵词汇表并不能帮我更快地学会日语。

sentences.en: What I needed was a different approach. And those different approaches included things like learning vocabulary in context, using spaced repetition, or reading more, listening to podcasts, I don’t know, using words in conversations.
sentences.zh: 我需要的是一种不同的方法。而这些不同的方法包括在语境中学习词汇、使用间隔重复法、或者多阅读、听播客、或者在对话中使用单词等等。

sentences.en: All of those things are not the same as working harder.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情并不等同于更加努力地工作。

sentences.en: They’re working differently, doing a different approach.
sentences.zh: 它们是换一种方式工作，采用不同的方法。

sentences.en: I realized my days of vocabulary study using my textbook wasn’t working very well for me.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我过去用课本背单词的日子并没有给我带来很好的效果。

sentences.en: It worked when I was a beginner, but not so much as I’ve become more advanced.
sentences.zh: 自我刚开始学时它挺管用，但随着我变得更加高级，它就没那么好用了。

sentences.en: I found it quite useful in my own studying journey to be a bit reflective and question my ability, question myself and my performance, and not just rely on the methods that worked for me 10 years ago today.
sentences.zh: 我发现在我自己的学习历程中，进行一些反思，质疑自己的能力、质疑自己和表现，而不是仅仅依赖 10 年前对我有用的方法，是非常有用的。

sentences.en: 10 years ago, I learned so quickly. Today, I don’t learn as quickly.
sentences.zh: 10 年前，我学得非常快。今天，我学得没那么快了。

sentences.en: The methods I need today are different from the methods I needed 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我今天需要的方法与 10 年前我需要的方法不同。

sentences.en: I try to ask myself… what kind of mistakes do I make?
sentences.zh: 我试着问自己……我犯的是什么类型的错误？

sentences.en: And am I learning from those mistakes? Or is my current learning method effective?
sentences.zh: 我是否在从这些错误中吸取教训？或者我目前的学习方法是否有效？

sentences.en: How could I do things differently? Is there someone who could give me useful feedback?
sentences.zh: 我该如何用不同的方式做事？有没有谁能给我提供有用的反馈？

sentences.en: ‘Cause feedback is really important. A growth mindset involves being willing to change, right?
sentences.zh: 因为反馈真的很重要。成长型思维包含着愿意改变的意愿，对吧？

sentences.en: Being flexible. Adapt. Different language learners need different things.
sentences.zh: 保持灵活性。适应。不同的语言学习者需要不同的东西。

sentences.en: Some of you listening to me right now might benefit enormously from joining my conversation clubs for speaking practice, but not all of you will benefit.
sentences.zh: 现在听我说话的你们当中，有些人可能会从加入我的口语练习俱乐部中获得巨大收益，但并非所有人都会受益。

sentences.en: Some of you will, not all of you will. Some of you might be great at remembering vocabulary through flashcards, but not all of you will enjoy that approach.
sentences.zh: 你们有些人会，但并非所有人都会。你们有些人可能很擅长通过闪卡来记忆单词，但并非所有人都会喜欢这种方法。

sentences.en: Everyone needs different approaches. Everyone needs different strategies.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要不同的方法。每个人都需要不同的策略。

sentences.en: You have to find the approach that works for you.
sentences.zh: 你必须找到适合你的方法。

sentences.en: Feedback is so important. Whether it’s from a teacher or an app or, I don’t know the, the back of your textbook where you have your answers counts as a form of feedback.
sentences.zh: 反馈是如此重要。无论是来自老师、某个应用程序，还是课本后面的答案（它也算作一种反馈形式）。

sentences.en: Feedback tells us how well we’re doing something, and it tells us when we do something wrong and when we make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 反馈告诉我们事情做得有多好，它告诉我们什么时候做错了、什么时候犯了错。

sentences.en: Feedback is so important to improving. Having a growth mindset means accepting feedback and seeing it as constructive criticism.
sentences.zh: 反馈对于进步至关重要。拥有成长型思维意味着接受反馈，并将其视为建设性的批评。

sentences.en: Just because I say that, “Oh, you pronounce this word incorrectly,” does not mean I’m saying you’re bad at pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我说“哦，这个词你发音不准”，并不意味着我在说你的发音很差。

sentences.en: I’m helping you improve your pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 我是在帮你的忙，让你把发音练得更好。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting things about a growth mindset is that mindset is not permanent.
sentences.zh: 关于成长型思维最有趣的事情之一就是，思维方式并不是一成不变的。

sentences.en: We can change the way we think about our abilities, and you can also have different mindsets at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我们可以改变对自身能力的看法，而且你也可以同时拥有不同的思维方式。

sentences.en: I have a growth mindset when it comes to academic subjects like language learning and maths.
sentences.zh: 在语言学习和数学等学术科目上，我拥有成长型思维。

sentences.en: I have always thought that I can learn and get better.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为我可以学习并变得更好。

sentences.en: But I have a fixed mindset in things like my musical and artistic ability.
sentences.zh: 但在音乐和艺术能力等方面，我有着固定型思维。

sentences.en: I believe that I am bad at music and art, and I will never get better.
sentences.zh: 我相信自己在音乐和艺术方面很差劲，而且永远也不会变好。

sentences.en: This has stopped me from ever learning piano, right?
sentences.zh: 这阻止了我去学习钢琴，对吧？

sentences.en: Or improving my ability to draw because I have this fixed mindset that I will not get better.
sentences.zh: 或者提升我的绘画能力，因为我抱有“我不会变好”的固定型思维。

sentences.en: The reality is if I tried, if I practiced, I probably could improve my ability.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，如果我尝试了，如果我练习了，我的能力很可能是可以提高的。

sentences.en: I guess you need to reflect, we need to reflect, on where we have fixed mindsets.
sentences.zh: 我想我们需要反思，我们需要反思自己哪里存在固定型思维。

sentences.en: What part of our lives or which of our abilities do we consider to be fixed and which do we consider improvable?
sentences.zh: 我们生活的哪一部分或者我们的哪种能力被我们认为是不变的，而哪些又是我们认为可以提高的？

sentences.en: Because all abilities are improvable. I’ve been working around English education for a decade now.
sentences.zh: 因为所有的能力都是可以提高的。我从事英语教育工作已经有十年了。

sentences.en: Even though I don’t teach English anymore, I do this podcast.
sentences.zh: 尽管我不再教英语了，但我做这个播客。

sentences.en: I talk to many English learners every single week, and it’s really common for people to make absolute or fixed statements about their ability.
sentences.zh: 我每周都会和许多英语学习者交流，大家对自己的能力做出绝对化或固定的表述是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: It’s really common for people to say something like, “I’m not good at public speaking.” A tip to change your mindset here would be to add the word “yet” to this kind of sentence.
sentences.zh: 人们经常会说诸如“我不擅长公开演讲”之类的话。在这里改变思维方式的一个小技巧就是在这种句子中加上“yet（还）”这个词。

sentences.en: “I’m not good at public speaking, yet.” The word “yet” suggests that maybe right now you’re not the best, but you could be good in the future.
sentences.zh: “我还不擅长公开演讲。”“yet”这个词暗示着也许你现在不是最好的，但未来你可能会变得优秀。

sentences.en: This immediately changes you to a more of a growth mindset.
sentences.zh: 这会立刻将你的心态转变为更具成长型的思维。

sentences.en: “I’m not good at public speaking yet, but I will be good.”
sentences.zh: “我还不擅长公开演讲，但我会变得擅长的。”

sentences.en: If you can’t do something yet, you need to think about what you can do to get closer to being able to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在还不会做某事，你需要思考你能做些什么来离能够做到它更近一步。

sentences.en: Comparing yourself to other people can also create this kind of fixed mindset.
sentences.zh: 拿自己与他人进行比较也会产生这种固定型思维。

sentences.en: There will always be someone better than you.
sentences.zh: 总会有人比你更优秀。

sentences.en: That’s just the way the world is. There will almost always be someone better than you, someone who learns faster than you, someone seems more talented than you, someone who seems to be great at pronouncing words, someone who seems to be able to think in a more creative way than you.
sentences.zh: 世界就是这样的。几乎总是会有人比你更优秀，有人比你学得更快，有人看起来比你更有天赋，有人似乎非常擅长发音，有人似乎能以比你更有创造力的方式思考。

sentences.en: It’s better just to compare yourself to yourself.
sentences.zh: 最好还是拿现在的自己和过去的自己作比较。

sentences.en: Compare yourself to your past self Teachers also need to help develop a growth mindset, and quite a few of you listening are teachers.
sentences.zh: 与你过去的自己作比较。老师也需要帮助培养成长型思维，听我节目的听众里有不少人就是老师。

sentences.en: One way a teacher can develop or help develop growth mindsets is by focusing on the learning process rather than telling students that they are intelligent or talented.
sentences.zh: 老师培养或帮助培养成长型思维的一种方法是关注学习过程，而不是告诉学生他们很聪明或很有天赋。

sentences.en: If you say, “Wow, you’re really good at this.
sentences.zh: 如果你说：“哇，你真擅长这个。

sentences.en: You must be really intelligent,” you’re saying to a student that their ability is fixed.
sentences.zh: 你一定很聪明，”你就是在对学生说他们的能力是固定的。

sentences.en: It’s based on their innate talent, when the reality is they have worked hard to develop that skill.
sentences.zh: 这是建立在他们的先天才能之上的，而现实情况是他们为了培养这项技能付出了努力。

sentences.en: Focusing on the skill itself, focusing on their hard work, encourages them to work harder and get better.
sentences.zh: 关注技能本身，关注他们的刻苦努力，会鼓励他们更加努力并变得更好。

sentences.en: One of the things I really disliked when I was working in Japanese schools was when other teachers told students or classes that there was something that people didn’t have the ability to do.
sentences.zh: 我在日本学校工作时真的很不喜欢的一件事，就是其他老师告诉学生或班级说有些事情是人们没有能力做到的。

sentences.en: The example I can think of right now is, I always remember observing an American English teacher’s class where during a pronunciation lesson focusing on L-R minimal pairs, /l/, /r/ minimal pairs… river versus liver.
sentences.zh: 我现在能想到的例子是，我一直记得曾经观摩过一位美籍英语老师的课，当时是在上一堂专注于 L-R 最小对立体、/l/、/r/ 最小对立体的发音课……river（河流）与 liver（肝脏）。

sentences.en: Right versus light. He told students that Japanese people can’t pronounce the English letter R very well, R very well, so don’t worry about it.
sentences.zh: Right（右/对）与 light（光）。他告诉学生，日本人发不好英语字母 R 的音，R 发得很糟糕，所以不用担心。

sentences.en: Of course, some Japanese people do struggle with L, R distinctions because these sounds are not distinct in Japanese, but that does not mean they can’t improve, they can’t learn, or they can’t develop.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些日本人确实在 L 和 R 的区分上感到吃力，因为这些音在日语中没有区别，但这并不意味着他们不能进步、不能学习或不能发展。

sentences.en: Telling someone that they can’t do something because of their nationality, because they’re Japanese, leads to a fixed mindset, where that person will decide that there is no point practicing pronunciation because they can’t improve, when the reality is they can improve.
sentences.zh: 因为一个人的国籍（因为他们是日本人）而告诉他们做不到某事，会导致固定型思维，这个人就会认定练习发音毫无意义，因为他们无法进步，而现实情况是他们完全可以进步。

sentences.en: You can improve, and it’s important to develop in yourself a growth mindset.
sentences.zh: 你可以进步，在自己身上培养成长型思维是很重要的。

sentences.en: Remind yourself that you can improve. It’s not guaranteed you will improve, but you can improve.
sentences.zh: 提醒自己你可以进步。虽然不能保证你一定会进步，但你可以进步。

sentences.en: You always have the option, the ability, the opportunity to improve.
sentences.zh: 你始终拥有进步的选择、能力和机遇。

sentences.en: Does having a growth mindset matter? Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 拥有成长型思维重要吗？是的，我认为是的。

sentences.en: The biggest benefit to having a positive mindset, a growth mindset, is that it can help you respond to difficulty in a productive way.
sentences.zh: 拥有积极思维、成长型思维的最大好处在于，它能以富有成效的方式帮你应对困难。

sentences.en: When you encounter a challenge, when you fail, when you make a mistake, you’re going to learn from it rather than feel sad.
sentences.zh: 当你遇到挑战、当你失败、当你犯错时，你会从中吸取教训，而不是感到沮丧。

sentences.en: The same way of thinking can apply to anything you want to get better at.
sentences.zh: 同样的思维方式可以应用在你想要变得更好的任何事情上。

sentences.en: Having a growth mindset will help you study, get better at sport or music public speaking, developing new skills.
sentences.zh: 拥有成长型思维将有助于你学习、在体育或音乐、公开演讲方面取得进步，以及培养新技能。

sentences.en: Of course, people have different abilities, different limitations.
sentences.zh: 当然，人与人能力不同，局限性也不同。

sentences.en: Sometimes we need to make more effort to progress than other people.
sentences.zh: 有时候，我们需要比其他人付出更多的努力才能取得进展。

sentences.en: But your current ability is not the limit of your ability.
sentences.zh: 但你当前的能力并不等于你能力的极限。

sentences.en: You can always have the opportunity to improve.
sentences.zh: 你永远都有机会去取得进步。

sentences.en: But what do you think? What type of mindset do you have?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你拥有什么类型的思维方式？

sentences.en: Do you have a growth mindset? Do you have a fixed mindset?
sentences.zh: 你拥有成长型思维吗？还是固定型思维？

sentences.en: Are you a bit mixed? What part of your language learning ability do you think you can improve?
sentences.zh: 你是有点混合型吗？你认为自己语言学习能力的哪一部分可以改进？

sentences.en: And what part do you feel a bit more skeptical, pessimistic over?
sentences.zh: 而哪一部分又让你感到更加怀疑和悲观呢？
